points.t: Any **rash, ulcer, lump or creeping track** in someone who has travelled or migrated in the past year.
**Exposure-specific infections** (sandflies, mosquitoes, soil, water, animals) plus common UK conditions acquired abroad.
Full **travel and exposure history**, examine all skin, **exclude malaria the same day if febrile**, use UK tropical-medicine advice routes.

cause.lead: Mostly common things; the rare ones are the missed ones.
points: Common: insect-bite reactions, impetigo / cellulitis from scratched bites, sunburn, phototoxicity, tinea, pityriasis versicolor, contact / phytophotodermatitis.

Exposures: **sandflies** (leishmaniasis), **mosquitoes** (dengue, chikungunya, Zika), **beach / soil** (larva migrans, tungiasis, mycetoma), **ticks** (rickettsial eschar, Lyme), **fresh water** (cercarial dermatitis), **sexual contact** (syphilis, HIV).
Incubation windows: dengue ~4–10 days; CLM days–weeks; leishmaniasis 2 weeks–6+ months; leprosy and mycetoma **years**.

visuals.caption: Prevention advice for the next trip includes fine-mesh nets: sandflies pass through standard mosquito nets.
visuals.alt: Coarse net with sandfly versus fine mesh

points: **Moving itchy serpiginous track** → cutaneous larva migrans.
**Painless ulcer with rolled edge**, weeks–months after → cutaneous leishmaniasis.
**Fever, aches, flushing / ‘white islands’** → dengue, chikungunya, measles; exclude malaria.
**Numb pale or red patches, thick nerves** → leprosy.
**Black eschar** with fever → rickettsia. **Boil with a central pore that moves** → myiasis.

visuals.caption: Creeping itchy track on the foot after a tropical beach: cutaneous larva migrans.
Painless ‘volcano’ ulcer weeks after travel: think cutaneous leishmaniasis.
visuals.alt: Cross-section of a crusted crater ulcer

items.name: Dengue
items.t: White islands in a sea of red.

points: Where (rural, beach, forest), **when**, activities, bites, water / animal / sexual contact, treatment abroad, migration / VFR.
Whole skin, nodes, mucosa; test sensation in pale patches.
**Same-day malaria film / RDT** + FBC + specialist advice.
Tropical-medicine services for biopsy / PCR; photograph to share.

manage.lead: Treat the common, refer the exotic early.

points: Treat as usual, with review dates.
Refer early to ID / tropical medicine (e.g. HTD e-Referral, on-call tropical registrar).
**No NSAIDs or aspirin** in a febrile traveller until dengue considered.
**No steroid creams on undiagnosed tropical ulcers; no systemic steroids** if *Strongyloides* or TB possible without specialist input.
Remember notifiable diseases; next-trip advice: DEET 50%, cover up, footwear on beaches.

items.t: **Fever after travel to a malaria area**: same-day malaria testing, whatever the rash.
Dengue warning signs (abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding, lethargy).
Nasal or oral ulceration after leishmaniasis exposure.

pearls.t: **“Where have you been, and when?”** for every unexplained or non-healing lesion.
**Painless** ulcers or swellings are warnings: leishmaniasis, leprosy, Buruli, mycetoma.
Test sensation and palpate nerves in pale patches from leprosy-endemic countries.
